title: How “Context Poisoning” is Rotting Your Codebase in the Age of AI
summary:
A simple analytics page took 15 seconds to load because one request fired over 200 database queries. The cause: AI coding assistants copy the patterns they see in your codebase, so one bad habit spreads with every new feature, and over time it becomes disastrous.
This post walks through how it happened, and how one query fixed it.

title: A Software Engineer’s Intuition for Gradient Descent, Part 2: The Step Size
summary: Adam, RMSprop and Newton’s method all keep the same rule as plain gradient descent: step downhill. What they change is the step size: one number for everything, one number per parameter, or a full matrix. This post climbs that ladder one real problem at a time.

title: Forget the Formulas: An Intuitive Guide to Time Series Modeling (ARMA)
summary: Forget the Greek letters: an ARMA model is two forces. Inertia, where today follows yesterday, and echoes, where a past surprise keeps shaking the system for a while. Plus how to read the ACF and PACF plots to choose the model’s size.

title: Tigers, Ghosting, and Bayes’ Theorem
summary: The same roar in the dark means “tiger” in a forest temple and “the TV” on your couch at home. Bayes’ theorem is the tug-of-war between what you already believed and what you just saw, explained with tigers, ghosting, and the Monty Hall problem.

title: Logistic Regression is Just Linear Regression with a Midlife Crisis
summary: Why does classification suddenly bring sigmoid, cross-entropy and maximum likelihood? Each piece of logistic regression fixes one concrete problem with using linear regression to classify, until it couldn’t have been built any other way.

title: Mastering the Precision-Recall Trade-Off: A Tale of Customer Support and Real Estate
summary: Is a false alarm or a missed case worse? A support bot that must never miss an angry customer, and a house hunter who must never buy a bad house, push the same threshold in opposite directions.
